Consumer is basically ChatGPT and Google's market to lose in my opinion. ChatGPT already has 1B users and needs to get them to connect their favorite apps and use agents to do work. OpenAI is already pioneering new interaction patterns like voice. The biggest barriers to overcome are: 1) Normies not trusting AI and ChatGPT with full access to their apps and data. 2) Normies not realizing what ChatGPT is now capable of. In both cases, I think marketing and the right messaging are just as important as improving the product. Google Gemini also has almost 1B users and my gut is normies trust it more to connect to email, calendar, Workspace, Chrome, etc since it's all the same login. But Google is behind on 3rd plugins, browser use, and alot of other critical features. They need to make the Gemini app best in class and friendly for normies. They can just copy ChatGPT tbh except make improvements like not have 3 separate modes (ChatGPT/Work/Codex) that ChatGPT and Claude are stuck in. fwiw I don't think having acess to the best model is that important to normies vs. getting the user onboarding right. My non-AI pilled friends could care less about Sol vs Fable as long as the pricing is fair and the model can get their work done reliably.
This is (of course) a massive distraction but the game I dream of building with AI is a roguelike deckbuilder that has great graphics, gameplay, and story.

Codex team: If I am in Codex tab and say "schedule this task in the cloud" (it's a task that just uses plugins) is it actually going to schedule it in the cloud or I have to switch to ChatGPT Work to do this? It doesn't seem to work?

Pinned: I’ve noticed people are much clearer when they speak through new ideas than writing a doc on it. Somewhere between their mouth and the doc, the core idea gets buried as they try to add context, polish it and make it sound smart. So here’s what I ask my teams to do: record yourself explaining the idea exactly as you would to a friend, use ai to do basic cleanup but keep the rough original structure and flow. Share that doc.
